chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the right of the father upon his son?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Not calling him by his name, and not walking in front of him, and not sitting before him, and not letting him be insulted (by anyone).'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific etiquettes a son must observe towards his father according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) details the specific etiquette of *adab* a son must observe toward his father, highlighting four key prohibitions: not calling him by his own name, not walking ahead of him, not sitting before him, and not insulting him. These actions symbolize the preservation of the father's dignity and status within the family hierarchy, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on honoring parents as a direct path to divine pleasure.
